name: Gym Challenge
description: The gauntlet that turns a collection into a campaign. A gym is an ordered set of trainers ending in a leader, a type identity that tells the player what to prepare, and a badge that is granted exactly once. Progress through the gauntlet is checkpointed between trainers so a loss costs the current fight rather than the whole run, which is the difference between a difficulty spike and a wall. The badge is the durable product: it is what world gates read to decide whether a route is open, so it is emitted as its own event rather than being inferred from a win. Level caps are declared per gym and enforced on entry — the genre's oldest anti-grind rule, and one that has to be stated by the gym rather than by the creatures, since it is a property of the challenge.

inputs.name: gyms
inputs.description: Ordered gym definitions: id, type identity, trainer sequence, leader, badge granted and level cap. Required — the gauntlet is content, and a default would be a fictional region.

inputs.name: enforceLevelCap
inputs.description: Whether creatures above a gym's cap are benched for that challenge.

inputs.name: checkpointBetweenTrainers
inputs.description: Whether a loss returns the player to the last trainer rather than the gym door.

inputs.name: rematchAfterBadges
inputs.description: Badges required before leaders offer harder rematches. 0 disables rematches.

outputs.name: activeGym
outputs.description: The gym being challenged, or null.

outputs.name: badges
outputs.description: Badge ids earned, in the order they were granted.
